$description: Tokens the system needs that Figma has no place to hold. Authored here so that a design value still lives in exactly one place. The normalization of a Figma export never touches this file.

layer.$description: Stacking order: the named layer a component occupies when things overlap. Each layer is named for what it holds.

width.$description: Width of the expanded sidebar. Not a step on any primitive scale.

modal.$description: The greatest width of a modal at each size. Fixed frame widths in Figma with no variable behind them; they should become variables.

width.$description: Width of a drawer from the left or right edge. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Least width of the dropdown menu panel, which grows from it to fit its longest item on one line. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

max-width.$description: Greatest width of the dropdown menu panel: past it a long item's words wrap inside the panel. Not in Figma, which draws the panel at one width.

width.$description: Width of the command palette. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the search field in the wide app bar. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

narrow.$description: Width of Figma's phone frames, used for the narrow previews of components that reflow. Not a viewport step; the steps in the size foundation are the layout breakpoints.

width.$description: Width of the table of contents card. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it.
Width of the popover panel. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the control in a side-by-side field, the label taking the rest of the row. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

Width of the note beside, under or at the end of a button: beside it, the note stays there while this much room is left after the button and moves under it otherwise. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

date-min-width.$description: Least width of the date field beside the time field in a date and time picker; with less room the time field moves under it. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

time-width.$description: Width of the time field beside the date field in a date and time picker. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

sort-width.$description: Width of the sort list in a wide filter bar, beside the search field and the filters button. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

field-width.$description: Width of a field in a toolbar: the list that picks what the bar acts on, a search field, a time range. A fixed frame width in Figma (the Picker, the Filter tools' search) with no variable behind it; it should become one.

plot-height.$description: Height of a line or bar chart's plot, the grid lines and the marks between its value labels. A fixed frame height in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

donut.$description: Width and height of a donut chart's ring. A fixed frame size in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

progress-ring.$description: Width and height of a progress ring at each size. Fixed frame sizes in Figma with no variable behind them; they should become variables.

width.$description: Greatest width of the color area, which is square and fills the width it is given up to this. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the color picker panel. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

link-underline.$description: Thickness of the line under a link. Figma sets a text's underline as a plain number with no variable behind it, and this one is not a step on the width scale.
Gap between a link's words and the line under them. Figma sets a text's underline as a plain number with no variable behind it.

text-size.$description: The viewport width at and above which the text size context switches from min to max. Aliases an existing viewport step rather than introducing a new measurement.

layout.$description: The viewport width at and above which the page counts as wide for layout. Below it, components that reflow for narrow spaces take their narrow form. Aliases the same viewport step as the text-size switch, so the two change together.

side-columns.$description: The viewport width at and above which a documentation page has room for a column on each side of its content: the sidebar on one side, the table of contents on the other. Between the layout switch and this width the page keeps one side column: the table of contents moves into the page and the sidebar starts as its column of icons. Aliases an existing viewport step rather than introducing a new measurement.

bold.$description: Figma's primitives stop at semibold, but its components set titles and button labels in Geist Bold. It lives here rather than in Figma.

fallback.$description: What a browser draws each family in until its web font has arrived, or if it never does, so the page draws in a sans close to the real one and barely moves when the real one arrives. The token build writes each family's stack after it in every text style that names it; the bundle writes each stand-in face, a font already on the reader's device scaled and spaced to match, into the font style sheets. Geist and Funnel Display have a stand-in face for each weight the text styles use, so light and bold text wraps where it will once its own face arrives: the regular one at the family, each other weight in a group named as `font.weight` names it, Arial for the light to medium ones and Arial Bold for semibold and bold. Each face's width is measured against its Arial over the design system's own prose, with kerning, as Chromium, WebKit and Firefox set it (they agree to a thousandth); each face's heights are the family's, which every weight shares. Geist Mono has one face, against Courier New, as every weight of both is equally wide. Figma has no place for any of it.

stack.$description: What follows Geist in every text style that names it: its stand-in face, then the system's own.

local.$description: The fonts already on the reader's device that the stand-in face draws with: Arial, or Helvetica where Arial is missing.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so its regular weight is as wide as Geist's: the two measured over the design system's own prose, with each font's kerning, as a browser sets it.

ascent.$description: Geist's height above the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

descent.$description: Geist's depth below the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

line-gap.$description: Geist's extra room between lines, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

light.$description: The stand-in face for Geist Light, at the weight `font.weight.light` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so it is as wide as Geist Light, measured as the regular one is.

medium.$description: The stand-in face for Geist Medium, at the weight `font.weight.medium` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so it is as wide as Geist Medium, measured as the regular one is.

semibold.$description: The stand-in face for Geist Semibold, at the weight `font.weight.semibold` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

local.$description: Arial's bold face, or Helvetica's, so the stand-in's letters are shaped as heavy as Geist Semibold's.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial Bold so it is as wide as Geist Semibold, measured as the regular one is.

bold.$description: The stand-in face for Geist Bold, at the weight `font.weight.bold` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

local.$description: Arial's bold face, or Helvetica's, so the stand-in's letters are shaped as heavy as Geist Bold's.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial Bold so it is as wide as Geist Bold, measured as the regular one is.

stack.$description: What follows Funnel Display in every text style that names it: its stand-in face, then the system's own.

local.$description: The fonts already on the reader's device that the stand-in face draws with: Arial, or Helvetica where Arial is missing.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so its regular weight is as wide as Funnel Display's: the two measured over the design system's own prose, with each font's kerning, as a browser sets it.

ascent.$description: Funnel Display's height above the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

descent.$description: Funnel Display's depth below the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

line-gap.$description: Funnel Display's extra room between lines, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

light.$description: The stand-in face for Funnel Display Light, at the weight `font.weight.light` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so it is as wide as Funnel Display Light, measured as the regular one is.

medium.$description: The stand-in face for Funnel Display Medium, at the weight `font.weight.medium` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so it is as wide as Funnel Display Medium, measured as the regular one is.

semibold.$description: The stand-in face for Funnel Display Semibold, at the weight `font.weight.semibold` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

local.$description: Arial's bold face, or Helvetica's, so the stand-in's letters are shaped as heavy as Funnel Display Semibold's.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial Bold so it is as wide as Funnel Display Semibold, measured as the regular one is.

bold.$description: The stand-in face for Funnel Display Bold, at the weight `font.weight.bold` names. Its heights are the family's, scaled by this face's own size.

local.$description: Arial's bold face, or Helvetica's, so the stand-in's letters are shaped as heavy as Funnel Display Bold's.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial Bold so it is as wide as Funnel Display Bold, measured as the regular one is.

stack.$description: What follows Geist Mono in every text style that names it: its stand-in face, then the system's own.

local.$description: The fonts already on the reader's device that the stand-in face draws with: Courier New, or Courier where it is missing.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Courier New so its average letter is as wide as Geist Mono's.

ascent.$description: Geist Mono's height above the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

descent.$description: Geist Mono's depth below the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

line-gap.$description: Geist Mono's extra room between lines, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

typography.$description: Weight variants of the Figma text styles that Figma has no text style for; its components apply the weight as an override on top of the regular style. They live here, not in Figma.

body-lg-bold.$description: Body LG in bold: a title over body text.

heading-2xs-bold.$description: Heading 2XS in bold: drawer and modal titles.

body-md-bold.$description: Body MD in bold. Kept for the sites built on the system; the system's own components use semibold for button labels.

body-sm-bold.$description: Body SM in bold. Kept for the sites built on the system; the system's own components use semibold for small button labels.

body-md-semibold.$description: Body MD in semibold: button labels.

body-sm-semibold.$description: Body SM in semibold: small button labels.

body-lg-light.$description: Body LG in light: a section's or an opener's lede, where Figma sets Geist Light.

duration.$description: Raw durations, named by their length in milliseconds. Figma has no motion design, so they are authored here. Components never read these; they read a motion purpose.

easing.$description: Raw easing curves, named by the curve they are: deceleration and acceleration, and one, back-out, that overshoots a little and settles, for a small mark popping into place. Components never read these; they read a motion purpose.

quart-in-out.$description: Eases in and out more steeply than the cubic curve: slow to leave, quick through the middle, slow to land.

cubic-out.$description: A soft start and a gentle stop, without the long tail of the expo curve.

steep-out.$description: Starts at full speed and settles gently over most of its length.

standard.$description: A gentle start, a quick middle and a long soft stop: the curve most interface toolkits use by default.

ease-out.$description: The browser's own ease-out: a brisk start that slows evenly to its stop.

back-out.$description: Runs past its end by about a tenth and settles back, as a light spring does. The one curve that overshoots.

motion.$description: Motion by purpose (motion.{purpose}.{property}): timing is chosen by purpose, not taste. Each purpose pairs a duration with an easing. Under reduced motion components move less and more gently, not never: anything that travels (a slide, a rise or drop, a change of size or height, a sweep, a turn) lands at once, while opacity and color fades keep their purposes.

feedback.$description: Confirming a pointer or focus change: a color shift on hover, a tooltip appearing.

state.$description: A control changing state in place and able to change back: a switch thumb sliding, a caret turning, a progress bar growing.

enter.$description: Something arriving or opening over the page: a drawer sliding in, a modal or menu appearing.

exit.$description: Something leaving or closing. Shorter than entering, and accelerating away, so a dismissal never holds the reader up.

expand.$description: Content opening in place and pushing what follows down, then folding back the same way: an accordion's panel. The same time and curve both ways, so what follows never jumps at the end and a press halfway turns it round where it is. The content fades in from a slight blur as it opens.

blur.$description: How blurred the content is as it starts to open, and as it finishes closing.

fill.$description: A choice's mark filling as it is chosen, a checkbox's box or a radio's circle: the fill grows from a little smaller than the mark as it fades in, and shrinks back as it fades out. The same time and curve both ways.

draw.$description: A tick drawing itself in its box, from its start to its tip, once the box has nearly filled; unticked, it erases itself back the same way, without the wait.

delay.$description: How long the tick waits for the fill before it starts to draw.

pop.$description: A small mark popping into place, as a radio's dot does: it grows from nothing a little past its size and settles back, and shrinks away the same way.

fold.$description: A sidebar folding to its column of icons and unfolding again: its width, and the parts the column hides, move on one in-out curve both ways, so a press on the way turns it round where it is. The words fade into a slight blur in the first part of a fold, and come back from it in the last part of an unfold.

label-duration.$description: How long the words take to fade into the blur, or back out of it.

blur.$description: How blurred the words are as they finish fading out, and as they start fading in.

delay.$description: The delay added per item in a sequence. Keep a sequence short enough that the last item starts within half a second.

hover.$description: A panel that opens while a mouse rests on its opener (a site header's menus): how long the pointer must rest before it opens, so a pointer passing over does not open it, and how long it may be gone before it closes, so it can cross from the opener into the panel. Touch and keyboard never wait; they open on a press. A tooltip and a label's help wait their own delays and close after this close delay.

open-delay.$description: From the pointer arriving on the opener to the panel opening.

close-delay.$description: From the pointer leaving the opener and panel to the panel closing; coming back within it keeps the panel open.

hold.$description: A finger held on a place that offers a menu (a right-click menu on a touch screen): how long it must stay down before the menu opens, so a tap or the start of a scroll opens nothing.

delay.$description: From the finger touching down to the menu opening; lifting or scrolling before then opens nothing.

tooltip.$description: A tooltip showing while a mouse rests on its target: long enough that a pointer passing over a row of controls shows nothing. Keyboard focus shows it at once, and once one tooltip has shown the next shows at once as the pointer moves along the row. It closes after the hover close delay.

open-delay.$description: From the pointer coming to rest on the target to the tooltip showing.

help.$description: Help the reader points at to read (a label's info icon), shown while a mouse rests on it: shorter than a tooltip's wait, since pointing at it is asking for it, and still long enough that a pointer passing over shows nothing. Keyboard focus shows it at once. It closes after the hover close delay.

open-delay.$description: From the pointer coming to rest on the help's icon to the help showing.

scrollbar.$description: The scrollbar drawn over a part that scrolls inside itself: it shows while a mouse is over the part and while it scrolls, and stays this long after the last scroll before it fades, so a reader who scrolls with the wheel sees where they are.

hide-delay.$description: From the last scroll to the scrollbar starting to fade, while the pointer is not over the part.

marquee.$description: A continuous strip that scrolls on its own. Runs at a constant speed.

spin.$description: A ring that turns while something is worked on, with no known end: one whole turn per duration, at an even speed, again until the work is done. Stopped under reduced motion.

live-pulse.$description: The pulse of something really live, open or running. A state, never decoration.

loading.$description: A placeholder waiting for its content: the skeleton's sweep, from one edge to the other, again until the content arrives. Stopped under reduced motion.

cursor.$description: A blinking text cursor. Blinks in steps, not with a curve.

ambient.$description: Slow background drift the eye should never have to follow.

theme-wipe.$description: The new theme drawn over the page in a growing circle from the theme switch's option that was pressed, until it covers the window, the easing shaping how much of the page has changed. A little quicker than the ambient drift it was first drawn with. Under reduced motion the theme changes at once.

chart-entrance.$description: A chart drawing itself the first time it comes into view, once: bars grow from the baseline one after another, a line and its area are uncovered from the start of the plot to its end, a ring sweeps round from the top. Changes after that land at once. Stopped under reduced motion, when the chart is simply there.

grow-duration.$description: How long each bar takes to grow to its height.

reveal-duration.$description: How long a line takes to be uncovered across the plot, or a ring to sweep round.

stagger.$description: The wait added for each bar after the first.

stagger-span.$description: The longest the last bar waits: with many bars the wait per bar shrinks, so the last still starts within half a second.
